metaData.originalTitle: 当 Agent 真正走进复杂数据分析场景：DataClawBench 用 492 个真实任务，给前沿模型做了一次过程级体检
metaData.title: When Agents Truly Enter Complex Data Analysis Scenarios: DataClawBench Uses 492 Real-World Tasks for a Process-Level Examination of Frontier Models
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: DataClawBench is a data analysis evaluation benchmark based on 492 real-world financial think tank tasks. By retaining uncleaned data and hiding data source priors, it conducts a process-level evaluation of frontier large models, revealing their capability boundaries and failure modes in real exploratory analysis scenarios.
metaData.summary: This article, published by the Chen Chuan research group at Sun Yat-sen University in collaboration with the Southern Weekly Science and Technology Innovation Research Center, introduces the DataClawBench evaluation benchmark. The core innovation of this benchmark lies in preserving the "exploration burden" of real data analysis — data is not pre-cleaned, data sources and schemas are not specified, requiring the Agent to explore autonomously. The benchmark includes 492 tasks from real think tank consulting assignments, spanning three major domains: enterprise, industry, and policy. It provides three layers of annotation: unique objective answers, key milestones, and reference trajectories. Experiments evaluated 8 frontier LLM Agents, with results showing that the strongest model, Claude Opus 4.6, achieved an overall accuracy of only 63.4%, while all others fell below 50%. Through process-level evaluation, the article categorizes model failure modes into four types: Decisive, Persistent Procrastinator, Random Tester, and Quitter. It also finds that Agents typically lose analytical clues early on, and the reasons for failure are not only due to executing incorrect operations but also due to choosing the wrong stopping method after an operation fails.

mainPoints.point: DataClawBench evaluates Agent capabilities by preserving the "exploration burden" of real data environments.
mainPoints.explanation: Unlike existing benchmarks with simplified data environments, DataClawBench does not pre-specify data sources, provide complete schemas, or pre-clean data. It requires the Agent to autonomously explore and discover needed data in an unknown, noisy environment, more closely resembling real-world deployment scenarios.

mainPoints.point: Frontier LLM Agents are far from mature in real-world data analysis tasks.
mainPoints.explanation: The strongest model, Claude Opus 4.6, achieved an overall accuracy of only 63.4%, while the remaining 7 models all fell below 50%. There is a cliff-like drop from medium to hard difficulty, indicating this problem is far from solved.

mainPoints.point: Process-level evaluation reveals differences in failure modes that outcome-oriented evaluation cannot detect.
mainPoints.explanation: Through a three-axis cross-analysis of Acc × GPR × TPE, models are categorized into four types: Decisive, Persistent Procrastinator, Random Tester, and Quitter. The same incorrect answer can hide completely different process-level failure modes.

mainPoints.point: Agents typically lose analytical clues early on, and the reasons for failure are related to operation type and stopping method.
mainPoints.explanation: Most models fail at the first milestone; stronger models can cross the initial evidence acquisition stage before faltering. Agents lose clues not only because they execute incorrect operations but also because they choose the wrong stopping method after an operation fails — operations like aggregation counting easily produce seemingly plausible but incorrect answers.

keyQuotes: Real data analysis is never about "reading a table and outputting a few relevant numbers." It is essentially an open-ended workflow with high accuracy requirements.

For evaluation scores to truly predict real-world deployment performance, the Benchmark must retain the data burden as is; otherwise, high scores achieved in a lab setting are likely to revert to baseline upon deployment.
The same incorrect answer can hide completely different process-level failure modes.
An Agent loses analytical clues not only because it executes a wrong operation but also because it chooses the wrong stopping method after the operation fails.

relatedArticles.title: From Rejecting AI to Asking Agent First for Everything: DHH Says It's One of His Most Enjoyable Programming Moments, But the Golden Age for Programmers Is Ending
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Ruby on Rails creator DHH shares his shift from resisting AI to fully embracing an Agent-First programming workflow, believing AI is amplifying the value of senior engineers, but the 'golden age' for programmers may be coming to an end.

relatedArticles.title: Nanjing University Team Challenges High-Score Myth of Large Models: Human 90 Points, Strongest Model Only 49 Points
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The Nanjing University team led by Fu Chaoyou released the new video understanding benchmark Video-MME-v2, which, through an innovative three-tier capability system and group-level nonlinear scoring, reveals a significant gap between the current strongest video models and human experts under rigorous evaluation, and finds that the gains from 'Chain-of-Thought' are highly dependent on textual cues.

relatedArticles.title: Are Models No Longer Key? LangChain Founder: The Orchestration Framework Truly Determines Agent's Upper Limit
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: LangChain founder Harrison Chase suggests that as models become commoditized, the core competitiveness of Agents will lie in their orchestration framework, which consists of system prompts, planning tools, sub-agents, and file systems.

relatedArticles.title: 1,500 PRs, 0 Humans Coding: Codex-Driven Million-Line Internal Product Practice
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI shares its internal team's experience using Codex/GPT-5 to achieve 100% AI-generated code and deliver a million-line product within five months, revealing a new paradigm of Agent-driven software engineering.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Code Creator Reveals He's a Liu Cixin Superfan! No PRDs, No Job Titles: How Anthropic Consistently Launches AI Hits
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic engineer Boris Cherny reveals the inner workings of Claude Code development, sharing insights on 'prototype-driven' culture, Agentic workflow practices, and the inevitable shift of engineers toward becoming generalists in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: Life of a Token: Understanding How Large Models Generate Tokens Like Debugging Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Using the GPT-2 Small model as an example, this article traces the complete inference process for a specific input 'The capital of France is', dissecting each step of data transformation in the Transformer model—from tokenization and word embedding to self-attention, feed-forward networks, and final prediction—revealing the internal mechanisms of LLM token generation.
